      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Suggested opaque types, exhaustive enums, and asserting non-null error pointer in trace scope"

  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:3675592714",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL on vector size allows test execution to continue and access out-of-bounds indices, causing undefined behavior",
      "quote": "BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(states.size(), 11) is non-fatal, but the test checks states[0] through states[10] after this. So if the size check fails, the test still continues and may access out-of-bound items, ",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author fixed by making boost size check a hard requirement",
      "author_replies": ["c:5457530691"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5457530691",
      "status_by_quote": "made the boost size check a hard requirement."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3758299224",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "null error pointer causes successful evaluation to report SCRIPT_ERR_UNKNOWN_ERROR in trace end frames",
      "quote": "a null m_error makes a successful eval report SCRIPT_ERR_UNKNOWN_ERROR. The kernel path always passes &error, but in case any non-kernel callers want to use the tracer, would it make sense to assert i",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author fixed by adding assertion for passing in error",
      "author_replies": ["c:5457530691"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5457530691",
      "status_by_quote": "added the suggested assertion for passing in the error."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3893679920",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "test suite fails when compiled with ENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE=ON due to callback pushing into destroyed vector in subsequent tests",
      "quote": "Add ScriptTraceUnsetCallback() to avoid the next test case push into a destroyed vector. Test suite currently does not pass with the feature flag.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author fixed by unsetting the callback after trace tests complete",
      "author_replies": ["c:5480776417"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5480776417",
      "status_by_quote": "unsetting the callback after the trace tests are complete."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5499409957",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "EvalScript triggers an assertion failure when tracing is enabled if called with a null serror pointer (e.g. in CheckSignetBlockSolution)",
      "quote": "The tracing code assumes serror is non-null whenever a callback is registered, but EvalScript permits nullptr... This triggers the assertion assert(!m_callback || error);",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author pushed fix making error code optional instead of asserting",
      "author_replies": ["c:5813055297"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5813055297",
      "status_by_quote": "making the error code \"optional\" by encoding `-1` as a nullopt. This gets rid of the assertion"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5499715130",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "oversized scripts are rejected before ScriptTraceScope is instantiated, preventing BEGIN and END trace frames from being emitted",
      "quote": "EvalScript rejects oversized scripts before constructing ScriptTraceScope, so a registered callback receives neither BEGIN nor END.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author declined changing interpreter and noted kernel lib catches the length check",
      "author_replies": ["c:5813055297"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:5813055297",
      "status_by_quote": "I don't want to change anything in the interpreter in this pull request. When running through the kernel lib's script verification, the length check will already be caught accurately"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5822201480",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "tracer incorrectly reports control-flow opcodes inside inactive branches as skipped even though they are executed by the interpreter",
      "quote": "The tracer uses `fExec` to indicates whether the current conditional branch is active. But the interpreter needs to process control-flow opcodes even inside inactive branches... the tracer incorrectly reported it as skipped",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,

    }
